title: SLOs and Error Budgets You Can Actually Burn
objective: Derive two SLIs from existing metrics, publish an SLO with a time window for each, and show remaining error budget shrink after an induced failure.
whyThisMatters: An SLO that is never computed is a wish. Error budgets turn reliability into a number you can spend or defend — the difference between 'it felt down' and a decision you can take to a product conversation.
evidence: An SLO document with SLI formulas, targets, windows, and a sourced justification for each target
The PromQL (or equivalent) used to compute each SLI and the remaining error budget
Captured SLI and remaining-budget output at a healthy baseline, with numeric remaining budget
Captured SLI and remaining-budget output after an induced failure, showing a strictly smaller remaining budget
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: Each of the two SLIs is expressed as a named query that returns a ratio or percentage, not a raw count.
Each SLO names a target percentage and a time window (for example 99.5 percent over 7 days).
The after-failure remaining error budget is a number strictly less than the baseline remaining budget, shown in captured query output.
The SLO document names one concrete action that would be blocked or allowed if remaining budget reached zero.
